objectives: Collect reliable data safely while working in a group.
Construct simple distance vs time graphs.
Analyse journeys using the shapes on distance vs time graphs.

engage.title: MOTION SENSOR
engage.hook: A motion sensor draws a graph as Sally moves in front of it. What line would it draw if Sally stood still?

reveal.question: Distance on the up axis, time along the bottom. Sally does not move.
reveal.answer: A flat, horizontal line. Time goes on, but her distance does not change.

learn.heading: Shapes on a distance vs time graph
learn.imageDescription: Distance vs time graph of one journey with sections A to E: steady, stopped, faster, coming back, speeding up

features.label: A  Straight line going up
features.description: Moving away at a constant speed

features.label: D  Straight line going down
features.description: Constant speed, coming back towards the start

learn.instruction: Sketch each shape in your book and label what it means.

learn.heading: Speed from distance and time
learn.example: On a distance vs time graph, a steeper line means more distance in the same time: a higher speed. A pupil hops 10 m in 8 s: speed = 10 ÷ 8 = 1.25 m/s.

build.q: On a distance vs time graph, what does a flat (horizontal) line show?
options: A. The object is stationary.
B. The object is moving at a constant speed.
C. The object is speeding up.
D. The object is coming back to the start.
build.explanation: Time goes on but the distance does not change, so the object is not moving.
build.commonError: Thinking a flat line means a steady speed.

build.q: What does a straight line going up show?
options: A. The object is stationary.
B. The object is moving at a constant speed.
C. The object is speeding up.
D. The object is slowing down.
build.explanation: The same distance is covered every second, so the speed is constant.
build.commonError: Thinking any line going up means speeding up.

build.q: Two straight lines on the same graph. Which one shows the faster object?
options: A. the steeper line
B. the less steep line
C. the longer line
D. the line that starts higher
build.explanation: A steeper line covers more distance in the same time, so it is faster.

build.q: A straight line going DOWN towards the time axis shows the object is…
options: A. coming back towards the start at a constant speed
B. speeding up
C. stationary
D. moving further away
build.explanation: The distance from the start is getting smaller at a steady rate.
build.commonError: Thinking a line going down means slowing down.

options: A. speed = distance × time
B. speed = distance ÷ time
C. speed = time ÷ distance
D. speed = distance + time
build.explanation: Speed is the distance travelled each second.

build.q: How do you make your times for the hop more reliable?
options: A. Time it once, as quickly as possible.
B. Repeat it three times and work out the mean.
C. Use a longer measuring tape.
D. Let a different person hop each time.
build.explanation: Repeats and a mean reduce the effect of one bad reading.
build.commonError: Thinking one careful reading is enough.

build.heading: DISTANCE VS TIME OLYMPICS
build.intro: In groups, time how long each 'event' takes over 10 m, then calculate the speed.
steps: Measure a 10 m track with the tape measure and mark the start and finish.
One person does the event; one person times it with the stopwatch.
Events: hop, crab scuttle, heel to toe, walking backwards.
Repeat each event three times and work out the mean time.
Calculate the speed: distance ÷ mean time.
equipment: masking tape or cones to mark the track
build.warning: Keep the track clear of bags and chairs. Walk, do not run, back to the start.

questions.q: Which event was fastest? How can you tell from your results?
questions.a: The one with the shortest mean time over 10 m (highest speed).

questions.q: Why did you repeat each event three times?
questions.a: To spot odd results and calculate a mean, so the time is more reliable.

statements.text: A flat line on a distance vs time graph means the object is moving at a steady speed.
statements.correction: A flat line means the distance is not changing: the object is stationary.

statements.text: A steeper line means a faster speed.
A line going down means the object is slowing down.
statements.correction: A line going down means it is coming back towards the start.

statements.text: The graph shows the shape of the path the object took.
statements.correction: It shows distance against time, not the route.

developing.q: Complete the sentences: A flat line shows the object is ______. A straight line going up shows a ______ speed. A steeper line shows a ______ speed.
A pupil hops 10 m in 8 s. Calculate the speed.
Sketch a distance vs time graph: a person walks away at a steady speed, stops for 10 s, then walks back home at the same speed.
developing.a: A straight line going up; then a flat line (10 s); then a straight line going down to zero distance.

reaching.q: Pete drives to work but is stuck in traffic part of the way. Describe the shape of his distance vs time graph.
reaching.a: A steep straight line (driving), then a flat or nearly flat line (stuck in traffic), then a steep straight line again (driving).

reaching.q: Hop: 10 m in 8.2 s. Crab scuttle: 10 m in 12.5 s. Calculate both speeds and say which is faster.
reaching.a: Hop: 10 ÷ 8.2 = 1.22 m/s. Crab: 10 ÷ 12.5 = 0.80 m/s. The hop is faster.

reaching.q: Explain how you can tell from a distance vs time graph which part of a journey was fastest.
reaching.a: The steepest part of the line is fastest, because the most distance is covered in the least time.

mastering.q: A car travels at 60 km/h for 2 hours. It stops at a service station for 2 hours. It then travels 30 km in heavy traffic at 15 km/h. Calculate the total distance and total time, and describe the graph.
mastering.a: First part: 60 × 2 = 120 km. Last part: 30 ÷ 15 = 2 hours. Total: 150 km in 6 hours. Graph: steep line to 120 km at 2 h, flat line to 4 h, shallower line to 150 km at 6 h.

mastering.q: Calculate the average speed of the car over the whole journey.
A distance vs time graph curves and gets steeper. What is the object doing? Explain.
mastering.a: It is speeding up (accelerating): it covers more distance every second, so the line gets steeper.
